title: Rec league fixture board
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Design and build an offline fixture board for the coordinator of a casual six-team table tennis league. Meetings run on Thursdays with two tables and three 25-minute slots beginning at 6:30 p.m. Seed the board with teams named Birch, Chalk, Fern, Lark, Moss, and Reed. The coordinator needs to enter pairings, spot double bookings, change a pairing at the venue, and print an evening sheet players can read from several feet away. Schedule changes should survive closing the app. Start from an empty directory and choose the deliverables, implementation, and file layout. The ordinary workflow should run on one laptop using free local tools.

files.name: README.md
files.body:
# Thursday League fixture board

Open **index.html** in a regular browser window. Keep the three app files together. All graphics, styles, and scheduling logic are local.

The first launch opens the upcoming Thursday (today if Thursday) with an editable evening in which every team plays twice. Use the arrows beside the date to plan another Thursday. Each additional evening starts with six open table slots.

Select a pencil to change the two teams, or a plus to enter a pairing. Save pairing applies your changes. Clear pairing releases that table. The editor names teams already playing on the other table during the same slot and prevents saving a double booking. Close or press Escape to discard an unfinished edit.

Select **Print sheet** for a landscape evening sheet. Use A4 or Letter, default scale, and disable browser headers and footers for a clean venue copy.

Saved evenings live in this browser profile on this laptop. Reopen the same file in the same browser and use the date arrows to revisit them. Private windows, clearing browser data, or moving the app can make schedules unavailable.

If your browser restricts storage for local files, run `python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1` in this directory and open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Keep using the same address and port for that collection of schedules.

files.body:
# Thursday Fixtures

Open **index.html** in a regular Chrome window. Keep the three app files together. The board runs offline from the folder and needs no installation, server, or account.

1. Use the date field or the week arrows to select a Thursday. Each date has its own evening schedule.
2. Select **Add pairing** for a time and table, choose two teams, and select **Save pairing**. Select any scheduled match to change or clear it.
3. The schedule check flags teams booked on both tables in the same slot. The editor also flags the conflict while you pick teams. You can save a conflict temporarily while rearranging matches.
4. Select **Print evening sheet**. Use portrait, 100% scale, and turn off browser headers and footers. The one-page layout works on Letter or A4. Conflicts appear on the sheet if they are still present.

Changes save in the current browser profile. Reopen the same file from the same location in the same profile. Private browsing, switching profiles, moving the app, or clearing browser site data can make previously saved fixtures unavailable.
